title: feat(scripts): gate the metadata-admin designer string tables (objectui#8834)
body:
Fixes #8834

Executes the PM re-ruling in comment 5602455535: Q1 = **C**, Q2 = **A**, Q3 = **A as an addition**.

## The gap

`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` carries the Studio designer's own module-local string tables (~3600 lines of user-visible text) and **nothing** checked that the two halves of a pair follow each other:

| gate | why it was blind |
|---|---|
| `check:i18n-keys` | resolves call sites against the `en` **pack**, and classifies this module `module-local table` by declaration and skips it outright |
| `check:i18n-drift` | read the **ten locale packs**; this table is not one of them |
| the dead-keys sweep | asks about **dead** keys over the **union** of both halves, so a one-sided key is not a subject to it — and it runs in no workflow by design ("This is a REPORT, not a gate") |

So: change an English string, forget the Chinese one, and CI is fully green.

## Three legs, each in the mechanism that owns it

**1. `check:i18n-designer-parity` — new script, new `ci.yml` step (Q2 = A).**
State invariants over the whole table: `en` ⊆ `zh`, and placeholder parity over shared rows using `tFormat()`'s own regex. Landing spot A rather than the originally ruled dead-keys sweep, because that script is invoked in **no** workflow — a leg there could never be observed red, which is the disease this card exists to cure.

**2. Q1 = C — enforce one direction, report the other.**
`en` ⊆ `zh` is a hard gate and arrives green with an **empty exemption ledger** (en-only = 0). The 55 deliberate `zh`-only keys are handled by a **report-only subtraction** of three documented families, each carrying its reason and in-file citation on the same line — never in the gate. A wrong entry in a report costs one missing output line; a wrong entry in a gate's ledger silently disables the gate.

**3. Q3 = A — the designer table as a second population of `check:i18n-drift`.**
The only leg that can see the defect the card opens with (an `en` **value** changed, the `zh` row did not). Its per-key skip rule handles all 55 asymmetric keys with **zero ledger**. Key-set symmetry is *not* dropped: drift is explicit that added/removed keys are not its business.

## Measurements

**Table scope — the ruling's premise is CONFIRMED, so all three pairs are seeded.** Measured through the shipped extractor with none of its `the extractor is stale` throws loosened:

| pair | en | zh | en-only | placeholder mismatches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ENGINE_STRINGS` | 1657 | 1712 | 0 | 0 |
| `TYPE_LABELS` | 36 | 36 | 0 | 0 |
| `DOMAIN_LABELS` | 9 | 9 | 0 | 0 |

All 3369 + 72 + 18 values are plain `StringLiteral`s, so collecting values needs no new tolerance. The 55 `zh`-only keys partition exactly: `engine.flowNode.` 42 + `engine.enum.type.` 4 + `engine.packages.form.help.` 9, **residue 0**.

**One extractor, not two (⛔ measurement ②).** `collectDesignerKeys` gains an optional second argument — supplied source text + label, a caller-chosen `consts` list, `withValues`, and base-side `require` tolerance. Every existing call site is byte-identical; every default reproduces the previous behaviour. `changeset-guard.yml:63-72` records what a second copy of a reader cost this repo, and the drift gate was the recorded victim.

**The new gate carries its own pair list (⛔ measurement ③).** `DESIGNER_TABLE_CONSTS` is untouched — widening it would change the dead-keys sweep's own population, and `TYPE_LABELS_*` / `DOMAIN_LABELS_*` keys are bare identifiers that do not sit under `DESIGNER_KEY_ROOTS`. A pin test asserts the two lists are not the same object.

**Split permission — not needed.** Leg 3 was a **bounded addition**, not a restructure: one optional parameter on `findDrift` (defaulted, so the ten-pack call site is unchanged), one new reader, one population fold, one `analyzeDesigner`, one field in `readLedger`, and one block in the CLI. No existing function body was restructured.

## Every leg was OBSERVED RED

Each mutation was proved to land on disk (occurrence counts before/after) and restored byte-clean, proved by blob hash **and** an empty `git diff HEAD` — never by a bare `git checkout --` exit code.

| leg | mutation | observed |
|---|---|---|
| symmetry | inject a synthetic en-only key | **exit 1**, names `ENGINE_STRINGS engine.synthetic.enOnlyProbe` |
| symmetry | inject a zh-only key **inside** `engine.flowNode.` | **exit 0**; family count 42 → 43; **0 mentions** of the key anywhere in the output |
| symmetry | inject a zh-only key **outside** every family | **exit 0**; residue **names** it: `ENGINE_STRINGS: engine.synthetic.zhOnlyProbe` |
| placeholder | drop `{count}` from one zh value | **exit 1**, names the key **and** `MISSING from zh: {count}` |
| drift | change one `en` value in a **real scratch commit** | **exit 1**, names `ENGINE_STRINGS.engine.directory.description` |

The drift leg ran on a **real base↔head commit pair** (`2eb5f3093` → `dfbe9c2bf`), both sides read as git blobs, not a simulation. **Ablation on the same commit pair**: the drift gate exactly as it stands on `origin/main` returns

```
VERDICT command-exit=0
No en value changed in this range.
```

— the defect, reproduced. This branch's gate on the identical pair exits 1 and names the key. Negative control (`--base C1 --head C1`) exits 0.

After the run: `HEAD` back at `2eb5f3093`, working tree clean, `i18n.ts` blob `eecaf1110092ebfd66ad7afdae407c71235cfed6` — identical to before.

## Tests and gates run

- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-designer-table-parity.test.ts scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-en-drift.test.ts scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-dead-keys.test.ts` → **141 passed (3 files)**, at `2eb5f3093`. The new suite pins both enforced legs twice — as pure functions and end-to-end through the real CLI, so the exit code is observed rather than inferred.
- `pnpm check:i18n-designer-parity` → exit 0, `1702 shared key(s), 126 of them carrying a {placeholder}, 55 zh-only key(s) (55 in a documented family)`.
- `pnpm check:i18n-drift` (merge-base discovery, as CI runs it) → exit 0, both populations reported.
- `pnpm check:i18n-keys` → exit 0 (the sibling gate is undisturbed).
- `pnpm type-check:scripts`, `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `pnpm check:entry-guard`, `pnpm check:esm-specifiers`, `pnpm check:unreferenced-sources`, `pnpm check:changeset-presence` → all exit 0.
- `eslint` over the six touched source files → exit 0.

**One existing pin fired and was obeyed, not weakened.** `check-i18n-dead-keys.test.ts` asserts that no workflow file so much as spells that script's name. My first `ci.yml` comment did; the comment was reworded. The pin stands unchanged.

**Governed surface: NOT governed.** `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test PATHS (all nine diff paths)` → `NOT GOVERNED — none matched`, with `AGENTS.md` as the lit control (→ GOVERNED, so the probe can see governance).

`Clause-②: no` — the diff touches only `scripts/**`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and a root `package.json` script entry; no published package surface moves. `Contract-text:` AGENTS.md §9 Housekeeping: a changeset is owed when a released package's `src/`, its `files`-listed publish, or one of the eight publishing-contract fields moves. `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` measures it: `7 file(s) changed, 0 of them published source of a package the release covers, 0 of them a manifest whose published contract moved`. An empty-frontmatter changeset declares the non-release explicitly.

## Fences honoured

⛔ No semantic / "is it actually translated" check. ⛔ The table is **not** folded into the ten locale packs — it is a separate population. ⛔ None of the 55 missing `en` rows were added. ⛔ The extractor was not loosened to reach `TYPE_LABELS_*` / `DOMAIN_LABELS_*`; they parse under the unchanged rules, which is what made seeding all three pairs legitimate.
